steps.title: Check cupboards
steps.prompt: Inspect the cupboards: 1 Pasta · 100 g pack, 0 Tomatoes · tin, 1 Cheese · 50 g pack. Build the quantities already at home.
steps.teach: Compare each requested quantity with the cupboard or order. Build one item at a time.
steps.example: Need three tins and have one? Put two tins on the list.
steps.hint: Re-read the quantity beside each item, then check the total.
steps.worked: Match the stock shown in the cupboard list.

steps.title: Make a shopping list
steps.prompt: Plan needs 2 Pasta · 100 g pack, 2 Tomatoes · tin, 1 Cheese · 50 g pack. Use your cupboard stock and list only what is missing.
steps.teach: Compare each requested quantity with the cupboard or order. Build one item at a time.
steps.example: Need three tins and have one? Put two tins on the list.
steps.hint: Re-read the quantity beside each item, then check the total.
steps.worked: Pasta · 100 g pack: 2 − 1 = 1; Tomatoes · tin: 2 − 0 = 2; Cheese · 50 g pack: 1 − 1 = 0

steps.title: Travel to Supermarket
steps.prompt: Reach Supermarket by 09:35, with 5 minutes to walk. Current time 09:00. Choose the cheapest bus arriving in time.
steps.teach: Add walking time to arrival before comparing the deadline. Then compare fares of the services that work.
steps.example: Arrive at 09:10 plus a 10-minute walk: reach the destination at 09:20.
steps.hint: Check arrival plus walking for each service. Pick the cheapest eligible fare.
steps.worked: Bus A costs £1.00; arrival plus walking is 09:30. Bus B misses the deadline and Express C costs more.

steps.title: Choose the shopping
steps.prompt: Follow the saved list for Tomato pasta. Your shopping limit is £64.00. Select only the missing quantities.
steps.teach: Compare each requested quantity with the cupboard or order. Build one item at a time.
steps.example: Need three tins and have one? Put two tins on the list.
steps.hint: Re-read the quantity beside each item, then check the total.
steps.worked: The list costs £2.35; £61.65 of the shopping limit remains.

steps.title: Pay for Tomato pasta
steps.prompt: The Tomato pasta costs £2.35. Build the £5.00 payment.
steps.teach: Count in pence. £1 is 100p. Change is payment minus the bill.
steps.example: £5 paid for a £3.20 bill leaves £1.80 change.
steps.hint: Add the denominations in your tray and compare with the requested payment or change.
steps.worked: Make 500 pence with coins or notes.

steps.title: Collect change
steps.prompt: Paid £5.00 for £2.35. Build your change before leaving.
steps.teach: Count in pence. £1 is 100p. Change is payment minus the bill.
steps.example: £5 paid for a £3.20 bill leaves £1.80 change.
steps.hint: Add the denominations in your tray and compare with the requested payment or change.

steps.title: Return bus home
steps.prompt: Return home by 10:05, with 5 minutes to walk. Current time 09:30. Choose the cheapest bus arriving in time.
steps.teach: Add walking time to arrival before comparing the deadline. Then compare fares of the services that work.
steps.example: Arrive at 09:10 plus a 10-minute walk: reach the destination at 09:20.
steps.hint: Check arrival plus walking for each service. Pick the cheapest eligible fare.
steps.worked: Bus A costs £1.00; arrival plus walking is 10:00. Bus B misses the deadline and Express C costs more.

steps.title: Unpack the recipe ingredients
steps.prompt: Match each ingredient to its required quantity before cooking.
steps.teach: Match the meaning and units of each label to its destination. Each label is used once.
steps.example: A 500 ml bottle matches half a litre.
steps.hint: Check each destination against the information in the task.
steps.worked: Pasta · 100 g pack → 2 × Pasta · 100 g pack; Tomatoes · tin → 2 × Tomatoes · tin; Cheese · 50 g pack → 1 × Cheese · 50 g pack
steps.instruction: Tap a label, then its matching destination.

steps.title: Prepare Tomato pasta
steps.prompt: Arrange the preparation stages for Tomato pasta. Your recipe says: Read the recipe; then Boil the pasta water; then Stir in tomatoes and cheese.
steps.teach: Put the actions into a sensible sequence. Explain what must happen before the next step.
steps.example: First read a list, then collect items, then pay.
steps.hint: Read the supplied sequence, then place each action in its position.
steps.worked: Read the recipe → Boil the pasta water → Stir in tomatoes and cheese
steps.instruction: Arrange the preparation stages for Tomato pasta. Your recipe says: Read the recipe; then Boil the pasta water; then Stir in tomatoes and cheese.

steps.title: Measure for Tomato pasta
steps.prompt: For this Tomato pasta batch, measure 0.3 litres of water in the jug.
steps.teach: Use the correct units and read the model from zero. One litre equals 1,000 ml; one metre equals 100 cm.
steps.example: 0.25 litres is 250 ml. Half a metre is 50 cm.
steps.hint: Convert the requested quantity to the model’s units before adding or removing units.

steps.title: Set the cooking finish time
steps.prompt: Tomato pasta starts at 10:00. Cook for 12 minutes. Build the finishing time.
steps.teach: Add minutes to the starting time. Carry 60 minutes into the next hour.
steps.hint: Find the starting time, add the duration, and check the hour change.

steps.title: Serve and tidy
steps.prompt: The Tomato pasta is ready. Order the finish: serve, store spares, then wash up.
steps.teach: Put the actions into a sensible sequence. Explain what must happen before the next step.
steps.example: First read a list, then collect items, then pay.
steps.hint: Read the supplied sequence, then place each action in its position.
steps.worked: Serve the meal → Put away spare ingredients → Wash the equipment
steps.instruction: The Tomato pasta is ready. Order the finish: serve, store spares, then wash up.
